newsitem.title: UK: Guerrilla car bomb defused in Northern Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Guerrilla car bomb defused in Northern Ireland.

text.p: British forces defused a guerrilla car bomb left outside police headquarters in Northern Ireland's second city, Londonderry, on Thursday, police said.
"An Army technical officer has successfully defused a large car bomb outside Strand Road police station," a police spokesman told Reuters.

A telephone caller purporting to speak for a hardline republican dissident group, the Irish Continuity Army Council, told news media earlier that its members had planted a 600-pound (275-kilo) device.
The incident darkened hopes of an early end to violence that has loomed over political efforts to end years of strife in British-ruled Northern Ireland.

It was the second major guerrilla alert within a week in Londonderry, which has enjoyed calm since Irish Republican Army guerrillas and pro-British militants declared truces two years ago. The IRA, the province's main republical extremist group, ended its truce last February, setting off bombs in mainland Britain and at military bases in Germany and Northern Ireland.
